brief: Use the customer-support workflow above as a fictional system. Work entirely from the facts supplied here; do not connect to a real service. Draw the components and data flows from user interface through model, orchestrator, retrieval store, policy service, refund API, email service and audit store. Mark trust boundaries, identities, data classifications, external dependencies and every side effect. Identify a business owner, technical owner, data owner, security/policy owner and incident contact.
do: List at least eight assets, including model context, customer records, credentials, tool definitions, memory and audit evidence.
Identify at least five trust boundaries and state what crosses each boundary.
Classify each action as read, draft, reversible write or consequential write; assign an autonomy tier.
Write three measurable security requirements, including one that prevents a refund from committing without transaction-bound authorization.
Record assumptions, exclusions, owners and evidence needed before pilot approval.
done: System understanding: Complete boundary, actors, data and side effects
Control design: Independent, scoped, testable enforcement
Evidence and testing: Clear artifacts, negative tests and traceable results
Risk and communication: Prioritized risks, assumptions, owners and defensible decisions
Evidence: A one-page context diagram; asset and data inventory; owner matrix; autonomy/action table; and three testable requirements.
experienced: Apply it to a real agent your organization runs, using the real tools, identities and data.
example: A defensible answer places the model and retrieved documents in an untrusted reasoning zone; the refund service is behind a policy enforcement point. The user identity is propagated as a verified principal, but the agent has its own workload identity and a narrowly scoped delegation. The refund endpoint independently checks customer ownership, amount threshold, case status, fraud state, idempotency key and approval token. The email export path is a separate capability, not implicitly available to the refund workflow. Logs record proposal, policy decision, approver, tool identity, resource, outcome and correlation ID while redacting secrets. No single owner substitutes for the others: business owns purpose and risk acceptance; engineering operates the service; data owners define permitted use; security defines controls; incident response owns containment.
